title: Sounding natural
goal: React like a native speaker, check and soften with tag questions, add emphasis and attitude with small particles, use echo words and doubled words, ask people to repeat or slow down, and get round words you don't know.
intro:
You can have perfect grammar and still sound like a textbook. What makes Kannada sound *alive* is the small stuff: the ಅಬ್ಬಾ! and ಸಾಧ್ಯನೇ ಇಲ್ಲ! when a friend tells you news, the ಅಲ್ವಾ? and ತಾನೇ? that pull the listener in, the -ಏ, -ಊ and -ಓ endings that add emphasis and doubt, and playful echo words like ಕಾಫಿ-ಗೀಫಿ 'coffee or something'.

This unit also gives you survival tools for real conversations: asking people to slow down or repeat, asking what a word means, and talking your way round a word you've forgotten. Bengaluru Kannada mixes in English freely (ಫುಲ್ ಬ್ಯುಸಿ, ಸಿಂಪಲ್ ಆಗಿ, ಅಡ್ಜಸ್ಟ್ ಮಾಡ್ಕೊಳ್ಳಿ), so you'll learn to do that the way locals do: English word, Kannada grammar.

vocab.note: ಅಬ್ಬಾ, ಎಷ್ಟು ಜನ! 'wow, so many people!'; ಅಬ್ಬಾ, ಮುಗೀತು 'phew, it's over'.
When something suddenly makes sense. With a teasing tone: ಓಹೋ, ಹೀಗಾ ವಿಷಯ! 'oho, so that's what's going on!'
A softer ಹೌದಾ? Also ಹೀಗಾ? 'like this?'.

vocab.en: come off it! get away! (to a guy, informal)
vocab.note: To a woman: ಹೋಗೇ. Playful disbelief between friends; never to elders.

vocab.en: yes? huh? mm (on the phone, when listening)
vocab.note: Rising: 'huh? what?'; flat: 'yes, go on'. Also ಹೂಂ 'mm-hm'.
ಸೂಪರ್ ಆಗಿದೆ 'it's great'. Also ಸಕ್ಕತ್ (very Bengaluru) and ಮಸ್ತ್.
ಬರ್ತೀಯ ತಾನೇ? 'you're coming, right?'. Also means 'just (now)': ಈಗ ತಾನೇ 'just now'.

vocab.en: but hang on, I mean (opening an objection)
vocab.note: At the start of a sentence: ಅಲ್ಲಾ, ನೀನು ಯಾಕೆ...? 'but wait, why did you...?'. Not the same as ಅಲ್ಲ 'is not'.

vocab.en: at last, finally; anyway; as for
vocab.note: ಅಂತೂ ಬಂದ್ಯಲ್ಲ 'so you finally came'. ಅಂತೂ ಇಂತೂ 'somehow or other, at long last'.
Added to verbs and words when speaking to someone you call ನೀವು: ಹೇಳ್ರೀ 'tell me', ಬನ್ರೀ 'come', ಏನ್ರೀ? 'what is it?'. Also how many wives call their husband: ರೀ!
Typical of coastal Karnataka and older Mysuru speech: ಏನು ಮಾರಾಯ! 'what's this, man!'. Friendly, not rude.

vocab.en: never mind, let it go; anyway
vocab.note: Lit. 'let it go' (from ಹೋಗಲಿ). ಹೋಗ್ಲಿ ಬಿಡು 'forget it'; ಹೋಗ್ಲಿ, ಈಗ ಹೇಳು 'anyway, tell me now'.
At the end of a sentence it closes the matter: ಸುಮ್ಮನೆ ಕೇಳಿದೆ, ಅಷ್ಟೇ 'I was just asking, that's all'.
Doubled ಏನು: asks for a list. ಏನೇನು ಬೇಕು? 'what all do you need?'
Doubled ಯಾರು. Object: ಯಾರ್ಯಾರನ್ನ 'whom all'.
Doubled ಎಲ್ಲಿ; also 'everywhere': ಎಲ್ಲೆಲ್ಲೂ.
Sound word: ಪಟಪಟ ಮಾತಾಡು 'talk nineteen to the dozen', ಪಟಪಟ ಉತ್ತರ ಹೇಳು 'rattle off answers'.
ಗಬಗಬ ತಿನ್ನು 'wolf down'.
ಚಕಚಕ ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡು 'work briskly'.
ಫುಲ್ ಬ್ಯುಸಿ 'totally swamped', ಫುಲ್ ಖುಷಿ 'over the moon', ಫುಲ್ ಟ್ರಾಫಿಕ್ 'jammed'.
A rhyming pair: ಸಣ್ಣಪುಟ್ಟ ವಿಷಯ 'little things', ಸಣ್ಣಪುಟ್ಟ ಕೆಲಸ 'odd jobs'.
ಈ ಪದದ ಅರ್ಥ ಏನು? 'what does this word mean?'. Also 'verse, song' in old usage.
ಉಚ್ಚಾರ ಮಾಡು 'to pronounce'. Casually ಪ್ರನನ್ಸಿಯೇಷನ್.
ನಾಲಿಗೆ ತುದಿಯಲ್ಲಿದೆ 'it's on the tip of my tongue'.
ಮೂಗಿನ ತುದಿ 'tip of the nose', ರಸ್ತೆ ತುದಿ 'end of the road'.
ಸಿಂಪಲ್ ಆಗಿ ಹೇಳು 'say it simply'; ಅವರು ತುಂಬಾ ಸಿಂಪಲ್ 'they're very down-to-earth'.

phrases.en: I told you so! (lit. I said it, didn't I)

phrases.note: Careful form: ಬಂದೆಯಲ್ಲ. Polite: ಅಂತೂ ಬಂದ್ರಲ್ಲ!

phrases.en: Could you speak a bit more slowly? (polite)
What do you call this in Kannada?
phrases.note: ಏನಂತಾರೆ = ಏನು ಅಂತ ಅನ್ನುತ್ತಾರೆ 'what do they say'.

phrases.en: It's on the tip of my tongue, I can't remember it.

phrases.native: ನನ್ನ ಕನ್ನಡ ಅಷ್ಟು ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿಲ್ಲ, ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಅಡ್ಜಸ್ಟ್ ಮಾಡ್ಕೊಳ್ಳಿ
phrases.roman: nanna kannaḍa aṣṭu chennāgilla, svalpa aḍjasṭ māḍkoḷḷi
phrases.en: My Kannada isn't great, please bear with me.
phrases.note: ಅಡ್ಜಸ್ಟ್ ಮಾಡ್ಕೊಳ್ಳಿ 'please adjust' is Bengaluru's favourite way of asking for patience.

grammar.title: Tag questions: ಅಲ್ವಾ, ತಾನೇ, ಆಯ್ತಾ, and the knowing -ಅಲ್ಲ
grammar.body:
A tag turns a statement into a check and pulls the listener in. Kannada has a handful, each with its own job.

**ಅಲ್ವಾ?** (written ಅಲ್ಲವೇ?) 'isn't it? right?' is the all-purpose tag. It works after any statement, positive or negative: ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿದೆ ಅಲ್ವಾ? 'it's nice, isn't it?', ನೀನು ಮೈಸೂರಿನವನು ಅಲ್ವಾ? 'you're from Mysuru, aren't you?', ಅವನು ಬರಲ್ಲ ಅಲ್ವಾ? 'he isn't coming, is he?'. Unlike English, it never changes to match the verb.

**ತಾನೇ?** 'surely…, right?' expects a yes and sounds a bit more insistent: ನೀನು ಬರ್ತೀಯ ತಾನೇ? 'you ARE coming, right?', ದುಡ್ಡು ಕೊಟ್ಟೆ ತಾನೇ? 'you did pay, didn't you?'.

**ಆಯ್ತಾ? / ಸರೀನಾ?** 'OK?' goes after a request or instruction: ನಾಳೆ ಬೇಗ ಬಾ, ಆಯ್ತಾ? The answer is ಆಯ್ತು or ಸರಿ.

**ಹೌದಾ? / ಹಾಗಾ?** 'really? is that so?' is the reply to someone else's news; ಹೌದು ಮತ್ತೆ! 'of course! exactly!' agrees strongly.

**A negative question as a nudge**: ಬರಲ್ವಾ? 'aren't you coming?', ಊಟ ಮಾಡಲ್ವಾ? 'won't you eat?'. This is the warm Kannada way to invite or urge someone.

**The knowing -ಅಲ್ಲ**: attached to a verb with no question intonation, -ಅಲ್ಲ means 'you know / after all / didn't I?': ಹೇಳಿದ್ನಲ್ಲ 'I told you, didn't I', ನೀನೇ ಹೇಳಿದ್ಯಲ್ಲ 'you said so yourself!', ಅಂತೂ ಬಂದ್ಯಲ್ಲ 'so you came after all!'.

**Intonation**: a tag goes *up* when you're really asking and *down* when you just want a nod.

examples.en: It's really muggy today, isn't it?
He's your younger brother, isn't he?
You did get the tickets, right?
I told you so at the start, didn't I!

grammar.title: Emphasis and attitude: -ಏ, -ಊ, -ಓ, ಅಂತೂ, ರೀ and friends
grammar.body:
Tiny endings carry a lot of attitude in spoken Kannada.

**-ಏ 'exactly, the very, only'**: ನಾನೇ ಮಾಡ್ತೀನಿ 'I'll do it myself', ಇವತ್ತೇ 'today itself', ಅದೇ! 'exactly!', ಅದಕ್ಕೇ 'that's exactly why'. In speech a noun ending in a vowel picks up ನ before it (ಕತೆನೇ ಇಲ್ಲ 'there's no story at all', ನಿದ್ದೆನೇ ಬರಲ್ಲ 'I can't sleep at all'); after a consonant it simply joins on: ಫೋನೇ ಎತ್ತಲ್ಲ 'he doesn't even pick up the phone'.

**-ಊ 'also, even'**: ನಾನೂ 'me too', ಅವಳೂ 'she too'. With a negative it means 'not even / no-': ಒಬ್ಬರೂ ಇರಲಿಲ್ಲ 'not a single person was there', ಏನೂ ಗೊತ್ತಿಲ್ಲ 'I don't know anything'.

**-ಓ 'some-, or, I wonder'**: ಯಾರೋ 'someone', ಏನೋ 'something', ಎಲ್ಲೋ 'somewhere'; ಏನೋ ಒಂದು 'something or other'. At the end of a sentence it adds doubt: ಬರ್ತಾನೋ ಏನೋ 'who knows whether he'll come'.

**ಅಂತೂ 'at last / anyway / as for'**: ಅಂತೂ ಮುಗೀತು 'finally it's over'; ಅಂತೂ ಇಂತೂ 'somehow, at long last'.

**Address words set the tone**:
• **ರೀ** with people you call ನೀವು, to sound friendly rather than stiff: ಹೇಳ್ರೀ 'tell me', ಏನ್ರೀ ಇದು? 'what on earth is this?'. It fuses with the verb: ಹೇಳಿ + ರೀ = ಹೇಳ್ರೀ.
• ಕಣೋ / ಕಣೇ (unit 21) with close friends; ಮಗಾ, ಗುರು between guys; **ಮಾರಾಯ** 'man' on the coast and among older speakers.
• -ಅಪ್ಪ / -ಅಮ್ಮ softens a request to anyone younger: ಹೇಳಪ್ಪ, ಬಾರಮ್ಮ.

**Openers and closers**: ಅಲ್ಲಾ... 'but hang on...', ನೋಡು... 'look...', ಮತ್ತೆ... 'so...', ಹೋಗ್ಲಿ 'anyway / never mind', ಅಷ್ಟೇ 'that's all'.

examples.native: ನಾನೇ ಫೋನ್ ಮಾಡ್ತೀನಿ, ನೀನು ಚಿಂತೆ ಮಾಡ್ಬೇಡ.
examples.roman: nānē phōn māḍtīni, nīnu chinte māḍbēḍa.
examples.en: I'll call them myself, don't you worry.
Not one person came to the party.
At last the exams are over!
What is this, I've been waiting for an hour!

grammar.title: Echo words and doubled words: ಕಾಫಿ-ಗೀಫಿ, ಬೇಗ ಬೇಗ, ಪಟಪಟ
grammar.body:
**Echo words: '… and stuff'.** Repeat a word, replacing its first syllable with **ಗಿ** (or **ಗೀ** if that syllable is long), to mean 'X and things like that'. It's casual and a little offhand:
ಕಾಫಿ → ಕಾಫಿ-ಗೀಫಿ 'coffee or something'
ಊಟ → ಊಟ-ಗೀಟ 'food and all'
ದುಡ್ಡು → ದುಡ್ಡು-ಗಿಡ್ಡು 'money and stuff'
ಸಿನಿಮಾ → ಸಿನಿಮಾ-ಗಿನಿಮಾ 'films and stuff'
ಊಟ-ಗೀಟ ಆಯ್ತಾ? 'have you eaten and all?', ದುಡ್ಡು-ಗಿಡ್ಡು ಏನೂ ಬೇಡ 'I don't want money or anything'. Some pairs are fixed rhymes: ಸಣ್ಣಪುಟ್ಟ 'small odds and ends'.

**Doubled words** do several jobs:
• hurry or intensity: ಬೇಗ ಬೇಗ 'quick, quick!', ಮತ್ತೆ ಮತ್ತೆ 'again and again', ಜಾಸ್ತಿ ಜಾಸ್ತಿ 'more and more'
• variety: ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆ 'all sorts of different', ದೊಡ್ಡ ದೊಡ್ಡ 'big (ones, plural)'
• lists: doubled question words ask 'which all': **ಯಾರ್ಯಾರು** ಬರ್ತಾರೆ? 'who all is coming?', **ಏನೇನು** ತಗೊಂಡೆ? 'what all did you buy?', **ಎಲ್ಲೆಲ್ಲಿ** ಹೋದ್ರಿ? 'where all did you go?'; numbers mean 'each': ಒಂದೊಂದು 'one each'.

**Sound words** (mostly doubled) paint a picture with a verb or with ಅಂತ: **ಪಟಪಟ** ಮಾತಾಡು 'rattle away', **ಗಬಗಬ** ತಿನ್ನು 'wolf down', **ಚಕಚಕ** ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡು 'work briskly', ಟಪ್ ಟಪ್ ಅಂತ 'drip, drip', ಢಂ ಅಂತ 'with a bang'.

examples.en: Come on, let's have a coffee or something.

examples.native: ಬೇಗ ಬೇಗ ರೆಡಿ ಆಗು, ಲೇಟ್ ಆಯ್ತು.
examples.roman: bēga bēga reḍi āgu, lēṭ āytu.

examples.en: Who all is coming to the wedding?
The kids rattled off the answers.
Give the kids a chocolate each.

dialogue.title: Big news over filter coffee
dialogue.setting: Emma, who has been learning Kannada for a year, meets her friend Kavya at a darshini in Jayanagar.

lines.native: ಏನೇ ಎಮ್ಮಾ, ಅಂತೂ ಬಂದ್ಯಲ್ಲ! ಕಾಫಿ-ಗೀಫಿ ಏನಾದ್ರೂ?
lines.roman: ēnē emmā, antū bandyalla! kāphi-gīphi ēnādrū?
lines.en: Hey Emma, so you finally made it! Coffee or something?

lines.native: ಹಾಂ, ಒಂದು ಫಿಲ್ಟರ್ ಕಾಫಿ. ಸಾರಿ, ಟ್ರಾಫಿಕ್ ಫುಲ್ ಜಾಮ್ ಆಗಿತ್ತು.
lines.roman: hāṃ, ondu philṭar kāphi. sāri, ṭrāphik phul jām āgittu.
lines.en: Yeah, a filter coffee. Sorry, the traffic was completely jammed.

lines.native: ಬೆಂಗಳೂರು ಟ್ರಾಫಿಕ್ ಅಲ್ವಾ, ಏನ್ ಮಾಡೋದು. ಸರಿ, ಕೇಳು, ಒಂದು ದೊಡ್ಡ ಸುದ್ದಿ ಇದೆ!
lines.roman: beṅgaḷūru ṭrāphik alvā, ēn māḍōdu. sari, kēḷu, ondu doḍḍa suddi ide!
lines.en: It's Bengaluru traffic, what can you do. OK, listen, I've got big news!
Rahul and Divya... are getting married, apparently!

lines.native: ಸಾಧ್ಯನೇ ಇಲ್ಲ! ಅವರು ದಿನಾ ಜಗಳ ಆಡ್ತಿದ್ರು ತಾನೇ?
lines.roman: sādhyanē illa! avaru dinā jagaḷa āḍtidru tānē?
lines.en: No way! They used to fight every single day, didn't they?

lines.native: ಹೌದು ಮತ್ತೆ! ಅದೇ ಎಲ್ಲರಿಗೂ ಶಾಕ್. ಹುಡುಗನ ಮನೆಯವರು ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ... ಏನಂತಾರೆ... ಆರ್ಥೊಡಾಕ್ಸ್.
lines.roman: haudu matte! adē ellarigū shāk. huḍugana maneyavaru svalpa... ēnantāre... ārthoḍāks.
lines.en: Exactly! That's what shocked everyone. And the boy's family is a bit... what do you call it... orthodox.

lines.native: ಒಂದು ನಿಮಿಷ, ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ನಿಧಾನವಾಗಿ ಹೇಳು. "ಹುಡುಗನ ಮನೆಯವರು" ಅಂದ್ರೆ?
lines.roman: ondu nimiṣa, svalpa nidhānavāgi hēḷu. "huḍugana maneyavaru" andre?
lines.en: Wait a minute, say it a bit slower. What does "huḍugana maneyavaru" mean?

lines.native: ಹುಡುಗನ ಫ್ಯಾಮಿಲಿ, ಅವನ ಅಪ್ಪ-ಅಮ್ಮ, ಎಲ್ಲಾ. ಗೊತ್ತಾಯ್ತಾ?
lines.roman: huḍugana phyāmili, avana appa-amma, ellā. gottāytā?
lines.en: The boy's family, his parents, all of them. Got it?
Oh, I see. Wow, what a story!

lines.native: ನಿನ್ನ ಕನ್ನಡ ಸಕ್ಕತ್ ಇಂಪ್ರೂವ್ ಆಗಿದೆ ಕಣೇ!
lines.roman: ninna kannaḍa sakkat imprūv āgide kaṇē!
lines.en: Your Kannada has improved so much!

lines.native: ಹೋಗೇ, ತಮಾಷೆ ಮಾಡ್ಬೇಡ. ಇನ್ನೂ ತುಂಬಾ ಪದ ನಾಲಿಗೆ ತುದಿಯಲ್ಲೇ ಇರುತ್ತೆ, ಬಾಯಿಗೆ ಬರಲ್ಲ!
lines.roman: hōgē, tamāṣe māḍbēḍa. innū tumbā pada nālige tudiyallē irutte, bāyige baralla!
lines.en: Come off it, don't tease me. Loads of words still get stuck on the tip of my tongue and won't come out!

lines.native: ಪರವಾಗಿಲ್ಲ, ನಿಧಾನವಾಗಿ ಬರುತ್ತೆ. ಮದುವೆಗೆ ನೀನೂ ಬರ್ತೀಯ ತಾನೇ?
lines.roman: paravāgilla, nidhānavāgi barutte. maduvege nīnū bartīya tānē?
lines.en: Don't worry, it'll come slowly. You're coming to the wedding too, right?

culture:
Kannada conversation is full of small sounds of agreement: on the phone people say ಹಾಂ, ಹೂಂ, ಹೌದಾ, ಸರಿ every few seconds, and silence can sound like you've stopped listening. Reactions are generous and dramatic among friends (ಅಯ್ಯೋ!, ಅಬ್ಬಾ!, ಸಾಧ್ಯನೇ ಇಲ್ಲ!), but with elders keep them gentle (ಹೌದಾ?, ಓಹೋ). Tags like ಅಲ್ವಾ? and ತಾನೇ? make you sound warm rather than pushy.

Bengaluru speech mixes English in constantly (ಫುಲ್ ಬ್ಯುಸಿ, ಸಿಂಪಲ್ ಆಗಿ, ಟೆನ್ಶನ್ ತಗೋಬೇಡ, ಅಡ್ಜಸ್ಟ್ ಮಾಡ್ಕೊಳ್ಳಿ), and nobody minds if you do the same, as long as the grammar around the word is Kannada. The words even differ by place: ಸಕ್ಕತ್ and ಮಗಾ are Bengaluru, ಮಾರಾಯ and ಉಂಟು are the coast, ಐತೆ and ಯಾಕ ಅಂದ್ರ belong to Hubballi-Dharwad. Locals love it when a newcomer tries, and you'll hear ಕನ್ನಡ ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿ ಮಾತಾಡ್ತೀರಾ! even when it isn't quite true yet. The polite way to ask for patience is ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಅಡ್ಜಸ್ಟ್ ಮಾಡ್ಕೊಳ್ಳಿ, and asking ಇದಕ್ಕೆ ಕನ್ನಡದಲ್ಲಿ ಏನಂತಾರೆ? almost always starts a friendly conversation.

tip.title: Reactions
tip.body:
- Surprise: **ಹೌದಾ? / ಹಾಗಾ?** (rising); strong: **ಸಾಧ್ಯನೇ ಇಲ್ಲ!** 'no way!'
- Understanding: **ಓಹೋ** 'oh, I see'; listening: **ಹಾಂ, ಹೂಂ**.
- Awe or relief: **ಅಬ್ಬಾ!** Pity: ಅಯ್ಯೋ ಪಾಪ. Annoyance: ಛೇ.
- Friendly disbelief: **ಹೋಗೋ** (to a guy) / **ಹೋಗೇ** (to a girl). Not with elders.

sentences.en: Is that so? I had no idea.
Oh, so that's why he didn't come today!
Wow, what a huge house!
Come off it, don't lie!
Huh? What did you say?
No way! He passed?
Your plan is brilliant!
Phew, I caught the bus, saved!
Really? Then I'll come too.

tip.title: Tags: ಅಲ್ವಾ? ತಾನೇ? ಆಯ್ತಾ?
tip.body:
- **ಅಲ್ವಾ?** 'isn't it? right?' after any statement; it never changes.
- **ತಾನೇ?** 'surely…, right?', expecting a yes: ಬರ್ತೀಯ ತಾನೇ?
- **ಆಯ್ತಾ?** 'OK?' after a request: ಬೇಗ ಬಾ, ಆಯ್ತಾ?
- **-ಅಲ್ಲ** with no question: 'didn't I / you know': ಹೇಳಿದ್**ನಲ್ಲ**!
- Nudge: negative question: ಊಟ ಮಾಡ**ಲ್ವಾ**?

sentences.en: This coffee is amazing, isn't it?
You've eaten, haven't you?
Tomorrow's a holiday, isn't it?
Call me once you get home, OK?
I told you he wouldn't come, didn't I!
You're coming too, aren't you?
Won't you eat? Come, sit down.
You said yourself the film was good!
But hang on, why did you tell him?
But why are you leaving so early?

tip.title: Little endings: -ಏ, -ಊ, -ಓ, ಅಂತೂ, ರೀ
tip.body:
- **-ಏ** 'the very, -self': **ನಾನೇ** ಮಾಡ್ತೀನಿ, ಇವತ್ತೇ, ಅದೇ!
- **-ಊ** 'too / not even': ನಾನೂ; ಒಬ್ಬ**ರೂ** ಇಲ್ಲ 'not a soul'.
- **-ಓ** 'some-, who knows': ಯಾರೋ, ಏನೋ; ಬರ್ತಾನೋ ಏನೋ.
- **ಅಂತೂ** 'at last'. **ರೀ** = friendly ನೀವು: ಹೇಳ್ರೀ. ಹೋಗ್ಲಿ 'anyway', ಅಷ್ಟೇ 'that's all'.

sentences.en: At last the rain's stopped!
I cooked it myself, how is it?
There was not a single person in the room.
Someone called you.
Who knows if he'll come, I've no idea.
Yes, tell me, what do you need?
What's up with you, man, you never even pick up the phone!
Never mind, let's see next time.
Just a coffee for me, that's all.
Exactly! That's just what I was saying too.

lessons.title: Coffee and stuff: echo words and doubled words

tip.title: Echo: ಕಾಫಿ-ಗೀಫಿ · doubled: ಬೇಗ ಬೇಗ, ಯಾರ್ಯಾರು
tip.body:
- Echo = repeat with **ಗಿ / ಗೀ** for 'and stuff': ಊಟ-**ಗೀ**ಟ, ದುಡ್ಡು-**ಗಿ**ಡ್ಡು.
- Double for hurry or variety: ಬೇಗ ಬೇಗ, ಮತ್ತೆ ಮತ್ತೆ, ಸಣ್ಣ ಸಣ್ಣ.
- Double a question word for a list: **ಯಾರ್ಯಾರು, ಏನೇನು, ಎಲ್ಲೆಲ್ಲಿ**; a number for 'each': ಒಂದೊಂದು.
- Sound words: **ಪಟಪಟ** ಮಾತಾಡು, **ಗಬಗಬ** ತಿನ್ನು.

sentences.en: Have you eaten and all?
No need for money or anything, just come.
What all did you buy at the market?
Who all have you invited to the party?

Give everyone a holige each.

lessons.title: When you can't find the word

tip.title: Getting round a missing word
tip.body:
- Buy time: **ಅದೇ… ಏನದು…** / **ಏನಂತಾರೆ…** 'what do you call it…'
- Describe it: '-ಓದು' 'the thing you…': ತಲೆಗೆ ಹಾಕೋದು; or **… ತರ** 'like a …'.
- Borrow the English word and give it Kannada grammar: ಇಂಪ್ರೂವ್ **ಆಗು**, **ಸಿಂಪಲ್ ಆಗಿ**, ಮಿಕ್ಸ್ **ಮಾಡು**.
- Then ask: ಅದಕ್ಕೆ ಕನ್ನಡದಲ್ಲಿ ಏನಂತಾರೆ?

new: ನನ್ನ ಕನ್ನಡ ಅಷ್ಟು ಚೆನ್ನಾಗಿಲ್ಲ, ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ಅಡ್ಜಸ್ಟ್ ಮಾಡ್ಕೊಳ್ಳಿ
